review_notes: I read the target file's simp-relevant definitions and their uses. These were `vlasovVectorField`, `clampToIcc`, `VlasovMeasureCurve.extend`, `supW1On` and the `wasserstein1_self` uses. I used grep to count the repeated unfold/rewrite patterns, and I read the Wasserstein.lean source of `wasserstein1_self`. The file has no `@[simp]` attributes at all. The three findings are missing canonical simp or equation lemmas. I found no competing-rule or looping problems. I did not run Lean, so none of the proposed lemmas has been compiled. WellPosedness.lean repeats the clamp-unfolding pattern, which suggests the lemma pays off downstream as well.

findings.excerpt: def clampToIcc (T t : ℝ) : ℝ := max 0 (min t T)
findings.problem: `clampToIcc` has no simp or equation lemma saying it is the identity on `Icc 0 T`. `VlasovMeasureCurve.extend` has no lemma saying `ρ.extend t = ρ.ρ t` on `Icc 0 T`. Every consumer therefore unfolds both definitions and redoes `rw [min_eq_left ht.2, max_eq_right ht.1]`. The proof `have h_clamp_eq : clampToIcc T t = t := by unfold clampToIcc; rw [min_eq_left ht.2, max_eq_right ht.1]` is copied about eight times in `Phi_step` and `Phi_step_envelope`. The `ρ.extend t = ρ.ρ t` proof (`unfold VlasovMeasureCurve.extend clampToIcc; congr 1; rw [...]`) is copied four times in those two theorems. The same blocks recur in WellPosedness.lean. The unfolding is also fragile: it exposes `max 0 (min t T)` and needs `congr 1`.
findings.proposed_change: After the definitions, add `@[simp] lemma clampToIcc_of_mem {T t : ℝ} (ht : t ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) T) : clampToIcc T t = t` (proof: `unfold clampToIcc; rw [min_eq_left ht.2, max_eq_right ht.1]`). Also add `lemma VlasovMeasureCurve.extend_of_mem (ρ) {t} (ht : t ∈ Set.Icc 0 T) : ρ.extend t = ρ.ρ t` (proof: `simp [VlasovMeasureCurve.extend, clampToIcc_of_mem ht]`). A simp lemma with a membership hypothesis can be discharged from a hypothesis `ht` in context, e.g. `simp [ht]`. Keep `clampToIcc`, `extend` and `clampToIcc_mem` reducible by unfolding only inside these lemmas. Then replace each `h_clamp_eq` / `h_eq` block with `simp [ht]` or `rw [clampToIcc_of_mem ht]`.
findings.benefit: Callers no longer unfold `clampToIcc` or `extend`, so definitions stay opaque and proofs stay robust. The clamp-then-identity normal form is stated once and used by `simp`. This removes about twelve duplicated proof blocks in this file and the same ones in WellPosedness.lean.

findings.problem: The definition has no `vlasovVectorField_apply`-style lemma, so the component form `(z.2, -(convolveFunctionMeasure gradW (ρ t) z.1))` is only reachable by unfolding. The file does this about 18 times: `unfold vlasovVectorField at hderiv` (lines 251, 873), `simp only [vlasovVectorField]` (lines 1378, 1550, 1923, 2667) and `simpa [vlasovVectorField] using h_proj` (lines 1465–2770, ten times). The projections `(vlasovVectorField ... z).1` and `.2` are also not simp-normalised. As a result every `HasDerivAt ... .1` and `.2` projection step needs a hand-written `simpa [vlasovVectorField]`.
findings.proposed_change: Add an equation lemma `lemma vlasovVectorField_apply (gradW ρ t z) : vlasovVectorField gradW ρ t z = (z.2, -(convolveFunctionMeasure gradW (ρ t) z.1)) := rfl`. Also add `@[simp] vlasovVectorField_fst` and `@[simp] vlasovVectorField_snd` for the two projections. Then `simpa using h_proj` and `rw [vlasovVectorField_apply] at hderiv` replace the unfold calls, and the definition itself need not be unfolded outside its own file section.
findings.benefit: The definition stays opaque. Projections of the vector field normalise to the force and velocity components with a single canonical rule, replacing repeated, definition-unfolding `simpa [vlasovVectorField]` calls with plain `simpa`. Later changes to the vector field's definition then affect only these three lemmas.

findings.declaration: supW1On_self and the `(wasserstein1 μ μ).toReal = 0` pattern (wasserstein1_self not simp)
findings.excerpt:
have h_self : (wasserstein1 (ρ.ρ s) (ρ.ρ s)).toReal = 0 := by
    rw [wasserstein1_self]; rfl
findings.problem: `wasserstein1_self : wasserstein1 μ μ = 0` is not tagged `@[simp]`, and neither is `supW1On_self` in this file. The `(wasserstein1 μ μ).toReal = 0` fact is therefore re-proved by hand with `rw [wasserstein1_self]; rfl` in `vlasovMeasureCurve_convCont` (line 4051), `constantCurve` (line 4192), `Phi_hW1Cont` (line 4835) and `picard_iterate_exists_limit` (lines 6505 and 6515). `supW1On_self` has to pass `wasserstein1_self` explicitly (`simp [wasserstein1_self]`, line 3858). Plain `simp` cannot close these goals, because `ENNReal.toReal 0 = 0` is only reachable once `wasserstein1_self` fires.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `wasserstein1_self` as `@[simp]` in Wasserstein.lean (its statement `wasserstein1 μ μ = 0` is a canonical, non-looping rewrite). Mark `supW1On_self` as `@[simp]` here. Then each `h_self` can be `by simp`, and `simp [wasserstein1_self]` in `supW1On_self` becomes plain `simp`. Alternatively, add `@[simp] lemma wasserstein1_self_toReal (μ) : (wasserstein1 μ μ).toReal = 0` next to it.
findings.benefit: A self-distance is the standard normal form `0`, so every later `simp` call that meets `wasserstein1 μ μ` or `supW1On S ρ ρ` simplifies it automatically. This removes five copies of the `rw … ; rfl` workaround.
